text:
Washington won on a night when its best goals came from its least likely shots. Justin Holl's go-ahead goal in the third period carried a 2% chance of going in, and Alex Tuch's slap shot shorthanded in the second was a 4% look. Tuch finished with two goals and an assist, and Washington's top line spent his shifts at 2.15 expected goals for against 0.61 against.

Montreal had the better of the first two periods by volume and quality. Josh Anderson scored twice, including a 28% chance in the second that tied it at 3, and the Canadiens led the game 68 to 52 in shot attempts. Lane Hutson had a goal and an assist while playing 24:12. But the Canadiens spent too much of the night chasing. Jakub Dobes allowed 1.8 goals more than the 23 shots he faced deserved, and WSH Charlie Lindgren was only slightly below expectation at minus 0.94.

The third period settled it. Washington out-chanced Montreal 2.70 to 0.68 in expected goals in the period, and Tom Wilson missed the net on a 41% look that would have made it even clearer. Holl broke the 3-3 tie, Tuch added a second goal at 17:05, and Nick Suzuki's power-play goal with 1:39 left only made the margin one. Over the full game, Washington's 4.42 expected goals to 3.06 gave it a narrow 52% claim to deserving the win.
